Understanding JavaScript SPA Rendering

By Jane Doe | March 10, 2026

Single-page applications (SPAs) have transformed how we build web applications. Unlike traditional multi-page websites, SPAs dynamically rewrite content without full page reloads.

How SPAs Work

At their core, SPAs use JavaScript frameworks like React, Vue, and Angular to render content on the client side. When a user navigates to a new "page," the framework intercepts the request and updates the DOM instead of fetching a new HTML document.

The Challenge for Web Scrapers

Traditional web scrapers send HTTP requests and parse the HTML response. But with SPAs, the initial HTML is often just a bare skeleton:

<div id="root"></div>

The actual content only appears after JavaScript executes. This means tools like curl or simple HTTP clients cannot access the rendered content.

Solutions

Headless browsers like Playwright can execute JavaScript and return the fully rendered DOM. Combined with content extraction libraries, we can reliably extract article content from any SPA.

  • Playwright renders the page with a real browser engine
  • Readability.js extracts the main article content
  • Turndown converts the HTML to clean Markdown

This pipeline provides LLM-ready Markdown output that preserves the document's semantic structure.
